items.prompt: White to move. The score says Nf3. The N is the knight and f3 is the square it lands on. Play that move.

claims.statement: The knight on g1 can go to f3.
The other knight cannot reach f3, so Nf3 names one move only.

hints: The first capital letter of a record names the piece. N is the knight (K is the king).
Two knights stand on the board. Which one can reach f3?
The knight on g1 jumps to f3.
items.explain: N is the knight and f3 is where it lands. Only the knight on g1 can reach f3, so Nf3 is a complete record.

items.prompt: White to move. The score says d4, with no capital letter in front. Play that move.

claims.statement: The pawn on d2 can go to d4.
A white pawn stands on d2.

hints: Look at the front of the record. Is there a piece letter?
A record with no capital letter in front is a pawn move. Which pawn can reach d4?
The pawn on d2 moves two squares.
items.explain: No letter means a pawn. The pawn on d2 moves to d4 (two squares, which a pawn may do from its starting square).

items.prompt: White to move. The score says exd5. The e is the file the pawn starts from and x marks a capture. Play that move.

claims.statement: The pawn on e4 can capture on d5.
A black pawn stands on d5, so the move is a capture.

hints: A pawn capture starts with the file the pawn leaves from. Which file is that?
The x says that something is captured. What stands on d5?
The pawn on e4 takes the pawn on d5.
items.explain: A pawn move has no piece letter, so a pawn capture names the file the pawn starts from: e. The x marks the capture on d5.

items.prompt: White to move. The score says Qxf7#. The x marks a capture and # means checkmate. Play that move.

claims.statement: Qxf7 is checkmate.
A black pawn stands on f7, so the move is a capture.
Two white pieces attack f7: the queen and the bishop.

hints: Q is the queen. Which square does it capture on?
The # sign says the move ends the game. Which pawn is the target?
The queen on h5 takes the pawn on f7.
items.explain: The queen takes the pawn on f7 (the x) and the game ends: # means checkmate. The bishop on c4 also attacks f7, so the black king cannot take the queen.

items.prompt: White to move. The score says O-O. That is the record for castling on the kingside. Play it by moving the king.

claims.statement: White can castle on the kingside.
The king goes to g1.
The rook goes to f1.

hints: This record has no piece letter and no square. It is a special sign.
O-O means castling on the kingside, the side of the h-file rook.
Move the king two squares to g1; the rook follows.
items.explain: O-O is castling on the kingside: the king goes to g1 and the rook jumps to f1. (Castling on the queenside is written O-O-O.)

items.prompt: White to move. Both white knights can reach d2. The score says Nbd2: the b says which knight. Play that move.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can go to d2.
The knight on f3 can also go to d2.

hints: Two knights could go to d2. The record must tell them apart.
The letter after N is the file the knight starts from.
The knight on the b-file, on b1, goes to d2.
items.explain: Both knights reach d2, so Nd2 alone would not say which one moves. The file letter fixes it: Nbd2 is the knight from b1, Nfd2 would be the knight from f3.

feedback_by_move.f3d2: That is the other knight, from f3. It would be written Nfd2.

items.prompt: White to move. The score says Bxf6. Tap two squares: where the bishop starts and where it lands.

claims.statement: The bishop on g5 can capture on f6.
A white bishop stands on g5.
A black knight stands on f6.

hints: B is the bishop. Which white bishop could capture something on f6?
The bishop lands on f6. Where does it come from?
The only white bishop that can reach f6 is the one on g5.
items.explain: B is a bishop and x a capture. The bishop on g5 takes the knight on f6, so the two squares are g5 and f6.

items.prompt: Black to move. The score says ...Nxd5 (the dots show it is Black's move). Tap two squares: where the knight starts and where it lands.

claims.statement: The knight on f6 can capture on d5.
The other black knight cannot reach d5.
A white pawn stands on d5.

hints: Black has two knights. Which one can reach d5?
The x says a piece is captured on d5. What stands there?
The knight on f6 takes the pawn on d5.
items.explain: Black has two knights, but only the one on f6 can reach d5, so Nxd5 needs no file letter. It starts on f6 and lands on d5, taking the pawn.

items.prompt: The board is turned: Black's pieces are at the bottom. White to move. The score says Bc4. Play that move.

claims.statement: The bishop on f1 can go to c4.
The other white bishop cannot reach c4.

hints: The names of the squares do not change when the board is turned. Find c4 by its file and rank.
B is the bishop. White's bishops start on c1 and f1; which one can reach c4?
The bishop on f1 goes to c4.
items.explain: Turning the board changes how it looks, not the square names. The bishop on f1 reaches c4; the bishop on c1 cannot.

items.prompt: Black to move. Play this score on the board, both sides: 1...d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3. The three dots show that the score starts with Black's move.

claims.statement: The first move of the score, ...d5, is legal.

hints: Each number counts a pair of moves. After 1... comes White's 2.c4.
Play one move at a time and say its record aloud: piece letter, then square.
Pawn moves have no letter: d5, c4, e6, e3. The others name their piece: Nc3, Nf6, Bg5, Be7.
items.explain: Eight moves, four by each side. Pawn moves have no letter; the knights and bishops are named by N and B. No x appears because nothing is captured.

items.prompt: White knights stand on b1 and h3. A score says Nd2. Is that enough to tell exactly which move was played? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can go to d2.
The knight on h3 cannot reach d2.

hints: Which white knights can reach d2?
Check each knight in turn: b1 and h3.
Only one of them can get to d2.
items.explain: Only the knight on b1 can reach d2, so Nd2 can mean only one move.

items.prompt: White knights stand on b1 and f3. A score says Nd2. Is that enough to tell exactly which move was played? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can reach d2.
The knight on f3 can also reach d2.
The knight on b1 can legally go to a3, c3 and d2.
The knight on f3 can legally go to d2, e5, g1, g5 and h4.

hints: Which white knights can reach d2?
Check each knight in turn: b1 and f3.
Both of them can get to d2.
items.explain: Both knights can reach d2, so Nd2 could mean two different moves. The record needs the file: Nbd2 or Nfd2.

items.prompt: White knights stand on b1 and h3. A score says Nd2! (the ! is a commentator's mark). Is that enough to tell exactly which move was played? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can reach d2.
The knight on h3 cannot reach d2.
The knight on b1 can legally go to a3, c3 and d2.

hints: Which white knights can reach d2?
A mark like ! or ? is the writer's opinion about the move. Does it change which move was played?
Only the knight on b1 can reach d2.
items.explain: Marks such as ! and ? are opinions added by the writer. They do not change which piece moved or where. Only the knight on b1 can reach d2, so Nd2! is one move.

items.prompt: White's rook on f1 goes to e1. Which record says exactly this move, in the fewest characters?

claims.statement: The rook on f1 can go to e1.
The rook on a1 can also go to e1, so Re1 is ambiguous.

hints: Which rooks can reach e1?
If more than one can, the record must say which one moves.
The moving rook starts on the f-file.
items.explain: Both rooks can reach e1, so Re1 would be ambiguous. The moving rook starts on the f-file, so the record is Rfe1.

items.prompt: White's rook on f1 goes to e1. Which record says exactly this move, in the fewest characters?

claims.statement: The rook on f1 can go to e1.
The rook on a2 cannot reach e1, so Re1 is not ambiguous.

hints: Which rooks can reach e1?
Add a file or rank letter only when two pieces could make the move.
Only the rook on f1 can reach e1.
items.explain: Only one rook can reach e1, so nothing needs to be added: Re1 is enough. Rfe1 is not wrong, but it says more than it has to.

items.prompt: Black to move. The score says ...Nbd7. Which knight moved?

claims.statement: The knight on b8 can go to d7.
The knight on f6 can also go to d7.

hints: Two black knights can reach d7. What does the letter after N tell you?
It is the file the knight starts on.
Which knight stands on the b-file?
items.explain: The b after N is the file the knight leaves from, so it is the knight on b8. The knight on f6 would be Nfd7.

items.prompt: White to move. The score says Rde1. Tap two squares: where the rook starts and where it lands.

claims.statement: The rook on d1 can go to e1.
The rook on f1 can also go to e1, which is why the d is needed.
A white rook stands on d1.

hints: There are two white rooks. What does the second letter tell you?
The d is the file the rook starts from.
The rook on the d-file, on d1, goes to e1.
items.explain: The letter after R is the file the rook leaves from: d. So the rook on d1 goes to e1; the rook on f1 would be Rfe1.
